memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD had said to Moses, 'Pharaoh will refuse to listen to you-so that my
wonders may be multiplied in Egypt.'" - Ex 11:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Moses in advance that Pharaoh will not listen. But look at the reason
given: "so that my wonders may be multiplied in Egypt."

This is one of those verses that makes us pause. Scripture holds two things
together here without embarrassment. Pharaoh genuinely hardened his own heart
(Ex 8:15, 8:32, 9:34), and God was sovereignly working out His purpose through
that hardening. Sincere believers have understood the relationship between these
two truths differently for centuries, and this devotional will not settle that
debate. What Exodus insists on is that both are true: Pharaoh is fully
responsible, and God is fully in control.

What this means practically is that Pharaoh's refusal did not defeat God's plan.
It became the stage on which God's power was displayed to Egypt, to Israel, and
to every generation since.

That is worth holding onto. The opposition you face is not outside God's reach.
The person who will not listen, the door that will not open, the situation that
will not move. God is not wringing His hands. Joseph's brothers meant evil, and
God meant it for good (Gen 50:20). The cross itself was the worst thing humans
ever did, and it became our salvation (Acts 2:23).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What closed door are you interpreting as God's failure?
2. Can you name a past refusal that God turned to good?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Sovereign Lord, nothing that resists You can defeat You. Help me to trust that
even the doors that stay shut are within Your hands. Amen.
